_comment: Pre-market brief. Regenerated on a schedule and committed; the site only renders it. See tools/market-brief.md for how it is produced and what each field must contain. Everything here is written in our own words from sourced reporting — do not paste licensed article text into this file.
headline: The hike landed. The bond market blinked first.
standfirst: Weekend edition. The Fed's unanimous 25bp on Wednesday took the Dow down 631 points; Thursday gave most of it back, with the S&P up 1.14% to 7,637.76, its best day since early August, as the ten-year fell to 4.93% from Tuesday's 5.04% high and oil slid. Friday's data is light — industrial production at 09:15 ET — and the weekend risk is the Iran war: Trump says he is near a decision on resuming large-scale strikes, and meets Gulf leaders on Tuesday.

bullets.title: A hawkish hike, priced, and the market still sold it
bullets.text: The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, the first increase since July 2023, on a 12–0 vote. The dots moved to 4.1% for end-2026 and end-2027, from 3.8% and 3.6% in June; 16 of 18 officials see at least one more hike this year, four see two. Growth was revised up to 2.3%, unemployment down to 4.1%, PCE to 3.7% and core PCE to 3.4%. Warsh said he was hard-pressed to call financial conditions restrictive and that summer inflation had not passed the test. The Dow fell 1.21% to 51,461.90, the S&P 0.45% to 7,551.81, and the two-year rose about 7bp.

bullets.title: Thursday reversed it, on semiconductors and a bond rally
bullets.text: The S&P rose 1.14% to 7,637.76, the Nasdaq 1.69% to 26,418.30 and the Dow 0.61% to 51,778.04. The Philadelphia semiconductor index gained 3.14% after Nvidia said chip sales would double next year; Intel rose 7.67%, AMD 6.4%, Arm 8.6%. Technology added 2.2% and every sector but financials and staples closed green. The ten-year fell 7bp to 4.93% and the two-year 5.4bp to 4.67%. For the week the S&P is down 0.3%, the Dow 1.5% and the Nasdaq up 0.3%.

bullets.title: Oil is heading for its first weekly loss in three
bullets.text: WTI is near $96 and Brent $103 after four-month highs above $102 and $107 on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia says it will restore about half the East-West pipeline within days and all of it within six weeks, is routing crude through Oman and shuttling it past the Strait of Hormuz; China has asked Iran to rein in the Houthis. Against that, the IRGC says it struck a tanker in the strait, Saudi–Houthi strikes widened on Thursday, and Trump says he is approaching a major decision on resuming large-scale attacks on Iran.

bullets.title: The Bank of England held and sterling fell anyway
bullets.text: Bank Rate stayed at 3.75% on a 6–3 vote, with three members including the chief economist voting for 4%. August CPI was 3.1%, a five-month high, and the Bank's own forecast has inflation above 4% in early 2027; it said risks are tilted further to the upside than in July. Markets price a 74% chance of a November hike. GBP/USD fell to 1.3336, its lowest since July, the FTSE 100 rose 1.2% and the ten-year gilt yield fell 8.1bp to 5.218%. The MPC also voted to run its gilt holdings down to zero by the end of 2034.

bullets.title: The Bank of Japan hiked to a 31-year high and the yen sold off
bullets.text: The policy rate went to 1.25% from 1.00% on a 7–2 vote, three months after the last move rather than six. Ueda said the phase of monetary policy has changed and the Bank will keep raising. The two dissenters were the prime minister's appointees, which analysts read as a limit on the pace. USD/JPY rose to about 157, up 1.18% on the day. Reuters' poll has 1.50% by end-March. The data behind all three central banks kept pointing one way: US retail sales rose 1.2% in August against 0.8% expected, jobless claims fell to 196,000 against 208,000, and the Atlanta Fed's Q3 nowcast is 5.1%.

calendar.note: Consensus +0.3% after +0.2%. Second-tier on a normal Friday; today it is the only US print, so it will get more of a reaction than it deserves.
Rarely moves price. Fed's Bowman speaks in London this morning; Lagarde spoke at 04:20 ET.

calendar.event: PBoC loan prime rate; Goolsbee and Lagarde speak
calendar.note: A quiet Monday. The week's risk is loaded onto Tuesday and Wednesday.

calendar.event: Trump meets Gulf leaders at the UN General Assembly
calendar.note: The post-war plan for Iran. Oil trades this headline; Saudi pipeline repair and Houthi strikes are the two inputs. KB Home reports after the close.

calendar.event: Flash September PMIs: eurozone, UK, US
calendar.note: US services printed 56.5 in August, the fastest expansion since 2020, and manufacturing 53.9. With a Fed that wants to see restriction, a strong flash is a hawkish print, not a growth cheer.

calendar.event: Jobless claims; new home sales at 10:00
calendar.note: Claims at 196,000 last week were distorted by Labor Day. A rebound toward 210,000 would be noise; a second sub-200,000 print would not.

calendar.event: Durable goods (August); Michigan sentiment final at 10:00
calendar.note: The one-year inflation expectation, 4.6% in the preliminary, matters more than the headline sentiment number now.
The print the Fed named. Core PCE was 3.3% year-over-year in July; the September dots assume 3.4% for the year. A 0.3% month is the number that makes December a second hike.

sessionNote: Friday after three central banks in 36 hours. The tape has had a three-day sell-off and a one-day rebound, and the rebound was narrow: semiconductors and the long bond, not breadth. There is no US release that can change the picture before Monday, so the session is about positioning into a weekend with an open war headline and a Tuesday summit. The clean window is the US morning after 09:15 ET; expect the afternoon to thin out and moves to exaggerate.
watchOut: The trap is reading Thursday as the turn. The ten-year at 4.95% this morning is flat, not falling; the two-year is up almost 2bp. A rally on lower yields that yields then stop delivering is a rally without a floor. The second trap is oil: it is down on Saudi repair headlines that can reverse on one strike, and the Trump decision on Iran is unscheduled. Size for the gap, not for the trend.

archive.headline: The ten-year touched 5% into the decision. The hike is not the event.
archive.summary: FOMC day. The 10-year had closed at 5.00% after touching 5.04%, the highest since 2007, with a 25bp hike priced at 92–94%. WTI had jumped 5.1% to $106.56 as fighting intensified in the Middle East; every US sector but energy closed red on Tuesday.

archive.headline: Core CPI ran hot into an FOMC that is now 90% priced to hike
archive.summary: Weekend edition. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected, PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year, and September hike odds moved from 61% to about 90%. Equities closed the week higher regardless — S&P +0.86% Friday, VIX −11% — while the 10-year finished at 4.96%.

archive.headline: Core CPI at a four-month high, hike odds jump to ~90%
archive.summary: Headline CPI held at 3.4% year-over-year but core rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected. Energy added 2.1% and gasoline 3.9%; airline fares rose 2.7%. Equities rallied regardless — S&P +0.86%, VIX −11% — while the 10-year touched 4.97%.

archive.headline: PPI beats, ECB hikes to 2.50%
archive.summary: August PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year against 5.3% expected with July revised up from flat. The ECB raised its deposit rate 25bp to 2.50% effective 16 September and cut its 2028 inflation forecast to 2.1%. September hike odds moved from 61% to 72%.

archive.headline: Oil tops $100, Dow sheds 400 more
archive.summary: Brent broke $100 for the first time since July and the 10-year yield hit a three-year high. Amgen fell over 10% on a failed cardiovascular trial and software names sold off. Barclays nonetheless lifted its year-end S&P target to 7,950.
